key_insight: SearchOS-V1 proposes a multi-agent search collaboration system that helps information-seeking agents stay on task when web search becomes long, noisy, or unproductive. Its core contribution is reducing repetitive search loops and improving robustness in open-domain evidence gathering.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the failure mode where single-agent and multi-agent LLM search systems lose track of progress over long interaction histories, repeatedly query unhelpful sources, waste search budget, and produce incomplete or lower-quality answers.
method: Introduces SearchOS as a system-level multi-agent collaboration framework for web-based information seeking.
Uses coordination mechanisms to track task progress and prevent agents from getting stuck in repetitive search loops.
Designs the system to improve robustness when searches fail, helping agents recover and continue toward evidence collection instead of retracing the same steps.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this matters because reliable search is foundational for retrieval-augmented and tool-using LLM applications. A more robust search workflow can improve answer completeness, reduce compute/search cost, and make agent systems more dependable in real-world open-domain tasks.
visual_elements: Multi-agent workflow diagram showing agents collaborating on search, evidence collection, and decision-making.
Loop-prevention illustration comparing naive repeated searches vs. SearchOS-guided progress tracking.
Pipeline graphic for information-seeking stages: query, search, evaluate, recover, synthesize.
Icon set for agents, web search, budget/cost, and evidence quality.
paper_title: SearchOS-V1: Towards Robust Open-Domain Information-Seeking Agent Collaboration
paper_authors: Yuyao Zhang, Junjie Gao, Zhengxian Wu, Jiaming Fan, Jin Zhang
